title: U.S. House · California's 52nd District
area: South San Diego County, including Chula Vista and the U.S.-Mexico border region.

context.text: The district's boundaries changed as a result of California Proposition 50, a mid-decade congressional redistricting measure voters approved on November 4, 2025.

Incumbent Juan Vargas and Jeff Belle advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, defeating Deborah Calhoun Rhodes and write-in candidate Frances Yasmeen Motiwalla. Vargas won 56.5% of the primary vote (71,608 votes) and Belle won 33.2% (42,090 votes).

candidates.name: Juan Vargas
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 56.5% of the vote.

summary.text: Juan Vargas is the Democratic incumbent U.S. Representative for California's 52nd District, first elected in 2012. A Harvard-trained attorney and former Jesuit, he served on the San Diego City Council, in the California State Assembly and in the California State Senate before entering Congress. He serves on the House Financial Services Committee.

background.text: According to his official biography, Vargas was born March 7, 1961, and raised on a chicken ranch in National City, one of ten children of Tomas and Celina Vargas; his father immigrated from Mexico in the late 1940s through the Bracero Program.
Earned a B.A. in political science from the University of San Diego in 1983 (magna cum laude), a Master of Humanities from Fordham University in 1987, and a J.D. from Harvard Law School in 1991.

As a young adult he entered the Jesuits, a Catholic religious order, and worked with disadvantaged communities, including orphaned children and displaced people in El Salvador, before leaving the order.
Returned to San Diego and worked as an attorney (associate) with the law firm Luce, Forward, Hamilton and Scripps.

Elected to the San Diego City Council in 1993 and served eight years; his office lists community-based policing, an after-school program, and "Operation Restore," a graffiti-removal and home-rehabilitation program employing homeless people, among his council initiatives.
Elected to the California State Assembly (79th District) in 2000 and served until 2006, where he was appointed Assistant Majority Leader in his first year.

After leaving the Assembly, worked as Vice President of External Affairs for Safeco Insurance and later Vice President of Corporate Legal for Liberty Mutual Group, according to his official biography.
Elected to the California State Senate (40th District) in 2010 and chaired its Banking and Financial Institutions Committee; served until 2013.
First elected to the U.S. House in 2012 and serves on the Committee on Financial Services. The district covers part of San Diego County and the U.S.-Mexico border.
Lives in San Diego with his wife, Adrienne, and has two daughters, according to his official biography.

priorities.text: Improving housing affordability in south San Diego County, citing long-standing support for Low Income Housing Tax Credits and tax credits for first-time homebuyers.
Comprehensive immigration reform addressing the root causes of migration and creating a pathway to citizenship for Dreamers, Temporary Protected Status holders, and farmworkers.
Combating climate change, citing work to safeguard clean air and water, create clean-energy jobs, and protect the region from wildfires and flooding.

positions.summary: Says the country needs stricter gun laws, citing his votes for the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act and to reinstate the federal Assault Weapons Ban, and support for raising the purchase age for semi-automatic rifles to 21 and banning bump stocks.
positions.quote: We need common sense public safety laws to reduce gun violence and stop this bloodshed.

positions.summary: Criticized President Trump's deployment of active-duty troops to the U.S.-Mexico border as a "political stunt," saying Congress needs pathways to citizenship and investment in asylum processing instead of enforcement actions aimed at "creating chaos and fear."
positions.quote: This decision to send active-duty troops to the border leads us down a very dark path. We need real solutions to fix our broken immigration system, not executive orders aimed at creating chaos and fear. We need pathways to citizenship, increased investments in asylum processing so cases can be more fairly and quickly adjudicated, and relief for families who have been separated.

positions.summary: Says he is fighting to restore and expand reproductive freedoms nationwide after the overturning of Roe v. Wade, saying a woman's medical decisions should be made with her doctor and her family.
positions.quote: I believe that a woman’s personal medical decisions should be made with her doctor and her family.

positions.summary: Says he is working to combat climate change, citing his support for the 2022 climate and clean-energy law and the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law's climate provisions.
positions.quote: I’m working to combat climate change to make sure we’re addressing this threat to our communities and our economy head-on; safeguarding clean air and water; creating good-paying clean energy jobs; and protecting our planet for future generations.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Financial Services for the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

Served on the House Committee on Foreign Affairs (Middle East, North Africa and Global Counterterrorism, and Western Hemisphere subcommittees) during the 117th Congress (2021-2022), in addition to the Committee on Financial Services.

candidates.researchNotes: Vargas has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey. Issue positions above are drawn from his official House website's Issues section, checked in this round of research.

candidates.name: Jeff Belle
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 33.2% of the vote.

summary.text: Jeff Belle is the Republican candidate for California's 52nd District, a Navy veteran who works as a consultant. In his Ballotpedia survey he describes himself as bringing federal and local government experience and says he is focused on affordability, immigration reform, and addressing Tijuana sewage pollution in the South Bay.

background.text: Attended Star Spencer High School and earned a high school diploma, according to Ballotpedia.
Served in the U.S. Navy from 1978 to 1980.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Oklahoma City University in 2019 and a graduate degree from the American Public University System in 2021.
Career experience includes working as a consultant; in his Candidate Connection survey he describes his background as combining federal experience and local experience, without further detail.

priorities.text: Addressing affordability in the South Bay through pro-housing supply policy, reduced permitting bureaucracy, and tax relief for working families, small businesses, veterans and seniors.
Addressing the Tijuana River pollution crisis affecting the South Bay.
Immigration reform combining secure borders, an updated legal immigration system, and a path for long-term undocumented immigrants who contribute to the country to gain legal status.

positions.summary: Says he supports building more housing and streamlining local permitting and regulation to increase housing supply and lower costs.
positions.quote: I support pro-housing supply, deregulation, and tax restraint over increasing taxes or restricting development to make living costs affordable. ... Build more housing to increase supply and lower costs.

positions.summary: Supports secure borders and enforcement against illegal entry and fraud, combined with a legal pathway and "earned legal 'First Priority' status" for long-term undocumented immigrants who contribute to the country.
positions.quote: My position supports secure borders, faster legal immigration, due process in asylum, respect human dignity, and earned legal “First Priority” status for long-term illegal immigrants who contribute to America.

candidates.researchNotes: Based on Belle's Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; no independent campaign website content could be retrieved in this environment.
